column8: Evidence of pyrethroid resistance in Anopheles amharicus and Anopheles arabiensis from Arjo- Didessa irrigation scheme, Ethiopia
column37: The study was conducted at Arjo-Didessa sugarcane irrigation area and its vicinity, Oromia Region, Ethiopia. According to a secondary source The area is found between two districts, Jimma-Arjo district and Buno-Bedele district in Oromia. The irrigation area has been classified into 11 agricultural commands, for this study, eight clusters were randomly selected for larval/pupal collection on the basis of anopheline larvae availability, larval density and habitat distribution. These were Com- mand-2, command-3, Command-4, Command-5, Command-6 and Abote Didessa (from the irrigation scheme), and from Kerka and Didessa clusters (clusters outside the irrigation area)
column41: According to a secondary source, LLIN and IRS were routine practiced and larval habitat management through community involvement was rarely applied except during epidemic years.
column95: According to a secondary source, the site was formerly a wildlife sanctuary (Didessa wildlife sanctuary), but since 2006 changed to a state-owned sugarcane plantation development to supply the sugar factory.
column291: The main habitat types in the irrigated clusters were manmade ponds, tyre tracks, sugarcane farm ditches, hippopotamus trenches, hoof prints of hippopotamus and seepages from irrigation canals and gate valves
